panels.title: Figure 3 (c): Accuracy of various max-token lengths (512 tokens, 1024 tokens, and input token length plus 512 tokens), illustrating the benefits of fair token allocation across questions.
notes: Grouped horizontal bar chart (matplotlib barh): 13 experiment settings on the y axis (top to bottom as listed in axes.y.ticks), three bars each, from the top: MT: 512 (blue), MT: 1024 (light blue), MT: 512plus (dark blue); the tick label sits at the first (MT: 512) bar and a gap separates the groups. Legend (right, inside the plot): MT: 512, MT: 1024, MT: 512plus. No number is printed at a bar: all 39 values are measured (source 'raster'). Rows are listed top to bottom, the three series in legend order, which is also their order in each group.

Measured on the figure's embedded bitmap (page 16: one RGB image of 1430 x 949 px with a soft mask, 3.06 px per PDF point, decoded from the PDF stream and composited on white). X calibration: least squares through the 6 tick marks under the axis (columns 243, 328, 412, 496, 581, 665 for 0, 10, ..., 50) -> 8.437 px per unit, 1 px = 0.119; fit residual at the ticks <= 0.05 (0.39 px).

Bar end = the last column of the bar's colour on a pixel row plus the coverage of the next column, median over the bar's 10 pixel rows (white dashed gridlines cross the bars, so each row was scanned from the right). In the rows of 'Comparative Analysis' the legend's colour patches (x 612-634) lie to the right of the bars; the bar ends there are at x 595.0, left of the legend box, and are fully visible. Estimated error +/- 0.06 (half a pixel).
Give Model Time to Think: MT: 512 rows y 381-390 end x 595.0 -> 41.63; MT: 1024 rows y 391-400 end x 637.4 -> 46.65; MT: 512plus rows y 401-411 end x 637.4 -> 46.65 (Table S4: 41.67 / 46.67 / 45.00)

Cross-check with Supplementary Table S4 (page 48; its rows are named Direct Questioning and Answer and Justify where the figure prints Direct Question and Answer Justification): the 26 MT: 512 and MT: 1024 bars equal the table's columns 'Max_token = 512' and '= 1024', largest |measured - table| = 0.07, including the one value that is not a multiple of 1/60 (Chain of Thought, 52.54 % = 31 of 59). All 39 measured values lie within 0.08 of n/60 in per cent (31/59 for that one bar).

The MT: 512plus bars do NOT follow the table's '512plus' column: in 12 of the 13 groups the dark bar is drawn exactly as long as the MT: 1024 bar above it (in 'Raw' it equals the MT: 512 bar). It agrees with the table in 4 rows (Expert Mimicry (44.95 vs 45.00); Contextual Embedding (43.29 vs 43.33); Answer Justification (49.93 vs 50.00); Option Analysis (43.29 vs 43.33)) and differs in 9 (Best Prompt (candidate 4) (44.95 vs 48.33); Give Model Time to Think (46.65 vs 45.00); Consensus Technique (43.29 vs 45.00); Confidence Scoring (53.37 vs 50.00); Comparative Analysis (41.63 vs 43.33); Elimination Method (46.65 vs 48.33); Chain of Thought (44.95 vs 41.67); Direct Question (48.29 vs 46.67); Raw (43.29 vs 45.00)). uncertain: Data chart with four panels (a-d), 75 rows: 6 + 39 bar ends, 12 + 18 interval centres with 24 + 32 interval ends. Nothing is printed at the marks, so every number is a raster measurement on the embedded bitmap; estimated error +/- 0.08 (a), 0.015 (b), 0.06 (c), 0.01-0.02 (d) axis units, far below 2 % of the axis ranges (1.4, 0.29, 1.1, 0.38).

Kinds: a and c are 'grouped_bar', b and d are 'forest' (a dot with a horizontal interval per row, as in the earlier truth for such plots); all four are 'horizontal', so the scorer normalises by axes.x.range, the measured extent of the plot area. A prediction that calls b or d 'scatter' or 'other' loses the kind match only. The scorer compares 'value' (bar end, interval centre); err_lo / err_hi are not scored.
Panel d has no legend: series is null and panel.series is empty, as the reading conventions ask; the scorer ignores series names when both sides have at most one. Panel b has two series on every row.

Panel d: the bars are drawn as mean ± SD although the legend text of the figure calls them 95 % CI; the truth records the drawn bar ends. Candidate 6 and Candidate 2 have no visible bar (err_lo / err_hi null).

Panel c: the dark MT: 512plus bars repeat the MT: 1024 bars in 12 of 13 groups and disagree with Supplementary Table S4 in 9; panel d: Chain of Thought and Elimination Method are plotted at other values than Supplementary Table S3 states. The truth keeps the plotted values (see the panel notes).
Values are the measured positions to 2 decimals, not rounded to the underlying fractions (n/60, n/180 or n/360 in per cent); the difference is at most 0.08.

Scorer name matching (names within 0.2 normalised edit distance count as equal, pairing is first-fit in row order): 'GPT3-API' and 'GPT4-API' (a) collide, the four categories 'Default - 10%' ... 'Default - 90%' (b) collide with each other, and the six 'Candidate N' (d) collide with each other. The truth lists rows top to bottom and series in legend order; a prediction in another order (GPT4-API before GPT3-API within a category, candidates 1 to 6 ascending) can be cross-paired and scored as wrong although its values are right.
No panel has a printed title (only the letters a-d): panel.title carries the panel's sentence of the figure legend printed under the caption on page 16.

bbox_px is the ink box of each panel (letter, labels, axes) mapped from the native bitmap to the bundle crop (1.5 px per PDF point from the picture bbox: crop_x = 0.4909 u - 2.97, crop_y = 0.4908 v - 4.83, checked on the plot-area edges within 0.5 px) and clipped to the 697 x 450 crop, which cuts the lower half of the x-axis titles of c and d. figure.bbox is copied verbatim from the picture's prov in document.json (l, t, r, b, origin bottom-left).
